column1: # Licence review of everything the AppImage bundles.
# One row per source package (Debian 13's, or our own build). The AppImage
# build maps every bundled file to its source package and fails on one that
# isn't listed here, or whose upstream version differs from the one reviewed
# (the part of `version` before the last '-'; a new Debian revision of the
# same upstream version doesn't need a new review). A new or updated package
# is read by hand -- the copyright file, and the source where it is unclear
# which files the shipped library is built from -- before it is added.
#   package   Debian source package, or the project for our own builds
#   version   the version reviewed (Debian source version)
#   ships     binary packages / components whose files are bundled
#   licence   SPDX expression for the parts we ship (not the whole source
#             package: tools, tests and docs are left out); LicenseRef-* for
#             licences SPDX has no id for, named as in the copyright file
#   offer     where the Corresponding Source is offered: `no` (permissive,
#             notices only), `snapshot` (linked by exact version on
#             doesn't have it or the licence doesn't allow a third-party server)
#   why       why it can be shipped inside a GPL-3.0-or-later program
# Every bundled package's copyright file is copied into the AppImage
# (usr/share/doc/orbis-reframe/licenses/), which carries the notices and the
# acknowledgements the permissive licences ask for.
# Where a package offers a choice of licences, the one named first in `why`
# is the one we distribute under. LGPL-2.1-or-later and GPL-2.0-or-later
# packages are distributed under their version-3 option, whose section 6(d)
# allows the source on a third-party server (snapshot.debian.org).
# Nothing here is GPL-2.0-only, which is what matters next to OpenSSL 3 and
# the other Apache-2.0 parts: Apache-2.0 is compatible with GPL-3 but not
